examples.en: Try pressing the screen lightly with your index finger.
I hurt my index finger when I fell.

examples.ko: 아이가 검지를 입에 대고 조용히 하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The child put a finger to his lips and told us to be quiet.
The ring is too big on my index finger.
I picked up the paper with my index finger and thumb.
The teacher pointed at the board with a finger.

explain: '검지'는 엄지 바로 옆 손가락이에요. '집게손가락'이라고도 해요. 순서는 엄지, 검지, 중지, 약지, 새끼손가락이고, 약속할 때 거는 손가락은 '새끼손가락'이에요.

phrases.en: I pointed over there with my index finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검지'와 같은 손가락을 가리키는 순우리말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word for the same finger as 검지.

phrases.en: The child pointed at the puppy with his index finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 가리킬 때 가장 자주 쓰는 손가락이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The finger most often used when pointing at something.
phrases.en_equiv: to point with the index finger

phrases.en: I picked up a small bead with my index finger and thumb.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 손가락으로 물건을 집을 때 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mentioned together when picking something up with two fingers.

explain_en: 검지 is the finger right next to the thumb, also called 집게손가락. The order is 엄지, 검지, 중지, 약지, 새끼손가락. The finger you hook for a promise is 새끼손가락.

examples.ko: 기타를 오래 쳐서 손가락에 굳은살이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I played guitar for a long time, so calluses formed on my fingers.

examples.ko: 발뒤꿈치 굳은살을 없애려고 따뜻한 물에 담갔어요.
examples.en: I soaked my feet in warm water to get rid of the calluses on my heels.

examples.ko: 일을 많이 하신 아버지의 손은 굳은살투성이예요.
examples.en: My father's hands, which have worked a lot, are full of calluses.

examples.ko: 굳은살은 너무 두꺼워지면 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: Calluses can hurt if they get too thick.
What soft hands, without any calluses.

examples.ko: 매일 연습한 사람만 이런 굳은살을 가질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only someone who practices every day can get calluses like these.

explain: '굳은살이 생기다', '굳은살이 박이다'처럼 말해요. 오래 연습하거나 일한 흔적이라서 '손에 굳은살이 박였어요' 하면 노력했다는 느낌도 있어요. 가운데에 단단한 심이 있는 '티눈'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: I walked a lot, so calluses formed on my feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생기다'보다 오랫동안 반복해서 단단해진 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like it hardened from long repetition than 생기다.

phrases.en: I shaved the calluses off my feet after the shower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 없애려고 직접 손질할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you trim them off yourself.

phrases.example: 운동을 열심히 해서 손바닥에 굳은살이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: I worked out a lot, so calluses formed on my palms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 어디에 생겼는지 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the body part in front to say where it is.

explain_en: You say '굳은살이 생기다' or '굳은살이 박이다'. Because it's a trace of long practice or work, '손에 굳은살이 박였어요' can also suggest hard effort. It differs from '티눈' (a corn), which has a hard core.

examples.en: I came out with a bare face today.
I was told I look prettier without makeup.
I don't want to show my bare face in front of my friends.
That actor's bare face looks very clear too.
I went out wearing only sunscreen on my bare face.
I posted a no-makeup photo and the response was good.

explain: 화장을 하지 않은 얼굴을 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '맨얼굴'도 많이 쓰는데, 둘 다 같은 뜻으로 말해도 괜찮아요. 보통 '민얼굴로 나가다', '민얼굴을 보이다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Shall I go out with a bare face today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장 없이 밖에 나가는 일을 말할 때 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, for going out without makeup.

phrases.en: A bare face is actually more comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민얼굴'과 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 둘 다 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '민얼굴'; both sound natural.

phrases.en: I'm shy about showing my bare face to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장하지 않은 모습을 남에게 보여 주는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing someone your face without makeup.

explain_en: It is used for a face with no makeup on. '맨얼굴' is a common alternative, and you can use either to mean the same thing. It usually appears in patterns like '민얼굴로 나가다' and '민얼굴을 보이다'.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my body is trembling.

examples.ko: 너무 화가 나서 손이 부들부들 떨렸어요.
examples.en: I was so angry that my hands were shaking.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 다리가 부들부들 떨려서 혼났어요.
examples.en: My legs were shaking before the presentation and I had a hard time.
The child was scared and spoke with a trembling voice.
The hand holding the coffee cup is quivering.

examples.ko: 그는 겁이 나서 부들부들 떨기만 했어요.
examples.en: He was frightened and could only tremble.

explain: 추위, 두려움, 화, 힘든 일 때문에 몸이 계속 떨리는 모양이에요. 거의 항상 '떨다'와 함께 써요. '덜덜', '벌벌'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: It was so cold that I shivered.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부들부들'과 비슷한 말이에요. 특히 추울 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 부들부들; used especially when someone is shaking from the cold.

phrases.en: I trembled with fear after watching a scary movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부들부들'과 비슷하지만 겁이 나서 떠는 모습에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 부들부들, but fits best when someone trembles out of fear.

phrases.en: I'm so nervous that my legs are trembling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떨다'는 내가 떠는 것이고, '떨리다'는 몸이 저절로 떨리는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 떨다 means you shake; 떨리다 feels like your body shakes on its own.

explain_en: It describes the body shaking continuously from cold, fear, anger or strain. It almost always goes with the verb '떨다'. '덜덜' and '벌벌' are used in similar ways.

examples.ko: 과일 껍질을 벗기니 하얀 속살이 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I peeled the fruit, white flesh appeared.
The skin that hasn't been in the sun is white.
I took out the clam's flesh and stir-fried it.
When you roast chestnuts, the yellow flesh is sweet.
Skin was visible through the torn pants.
The flesh of the potato turned brown.

explain: 옷이나 껍질 속에 감춰진 부드러운 부분이에요. 과일, 조개, 감자처럼 먹는 것의 안쪽에도 쓰고, 옷 속의 피부에도 써요. 피부를 말할 때는 보통 '맨살'이라고 하는 경우가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: When I peel the apple, I can see the white flesh.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일이나 생선처럼 먹는 것의 안쪽을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the inside of food such as fruit or fish.

phrases.en: The clothes are torn, so you can see the skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 속에 감춰진 피부가 드러날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when skin hidden under clothes shows.

phrases.en: I put lotion on my bare skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부를 말할 때는 '속살'보다 '맨살'이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For skin, '맨살' is more common than '속살'.

explain_en: The soft part hidden inside clothes or a skin. It is used for the inside of foods such as fruit, clams and potatoes, and also for skin under clothes. For bare skin, 맨살 is often the more usual word.

examples.en: I skipped breakfast, so I'm very hungry.
If you're hungry, please eat first.
It's past lunchtime, so I'm a bit hungry.
I served warm soup to the hungry guest.
He must have been really hungry; he ate in no time.

examples.ko: 시장할 때 먹는 밥이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: Rice eaten when you're hungry tastes best.

explain: '배고프다'가 보통 말이고, '시장하다'는 조금 점잖고 공손한 말이에요. 어른께 '시장하시지요?'처럼 물을 때 써요. 같은 소리의 '시장(market)'과는 관계가 없어요.

phrases.en: You've waited a long time, so you must be hungry, right?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른께 공손하게 물을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask an elder if they are hungry.

phrases.en: I skipped lunch, so I'm very hungry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시장하다'보다 편한 보통 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ordinary, casual word for hungry.

phrases.example: 조금 전에 먹어서 지금은 시장하지 않아요.
phrases.en: I ate a little while ago, so I'm not hungry now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 점잖게 거절할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, useful for politely declining food.

explain_en: '배고프다' is the normal word; '시장하다' is more polite and refined. You'd ask an elder '시장하시지요?'. It has nothing to do with '시장' (market).

en: to be loose; to be slack

examples.en: The shoes are loose, so it's uncomfortable to walk.
I may have lost weight; my pants feel loose.
I tightened the loose screw with a screwdriver.
The rope is tied too loosely.
The watch I bought yesterday was loose on my wrist.

examples.ko: 헐겁다고 느껴지면 한 사이즈 작은 걸 입어 보세요.
examples.en: If it feels loose, try a size smaller.

explain: 신발·옷·반지처럼 몸에 꼭 맞지 않고 남는 느낌일 때 써요. 반대로 꼭 맞거나 작으면 '꽉 끼다'라고 해요. 나사·줄처럼 단단히 조여 있지 않은 물건에도 쓰고, 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '헐거워요', '헐거운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Wearing loose shoes makes my feet hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 명사 앞에서는 '헐거운'으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes 헐거운 before a noun.

phrases.example: 이 반지는 헐겁지 않고 딱 맞아요.
phrases.en: This ring isn't loose; it fits perfectly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형은 '헐겁지 않아요'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is 헐겁지 않아요.

phrases.en: The screw got loose, so I need to tighten it again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'를 붙여 점점 느슨해지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -아/어지다 expresses a change toward looseness.

explain_en: It is used when shoes, clothes or rings don't fit snugly and feel too roomy. When something fits tightly or is too small, say '꽉 끼다'. It also applies to things not tightened firmly, like screws and ropes, and as a ㅂ-irregular it becomes '헐거워요' and '헐거운'.

examples.en: The soup is boiling on the stove.
Please turn down the stove heat.
I bought a new stove, and the kitchen looks clean.
The stove in my house runs on electricity.

examples.ko: 레인지가 고장 나서 수리 기사님을 불렀어요.
examples.en: The stove broke, so I called a repairman.

examples.ko: 요리하기 전에 레인지 주변을 먼저 닦았어요.
examples.en: I wiped around the stove before cooking.

explain: '레인지'는 '가스레인지'나 '전기레인지'(불이나 열로 요리하는 조리대)를 줄인 말이기도 하고, '전자레인지'를 줄인 말이기도 해요. 그래서 '레인지에 돌리다'는 보통 전자레인지를 뜻해요. 조리대를 말할 때는 헷갈리지 않게 '가스레인지', '전기레인지'처럼 앞말을 붙이는 편이 안전해요.

phrases.example: 가스레인지 불을 끄는 것을 잊지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't forget to turn off the gas stove.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가스로 불을 켜는 조리대를 말하고, '레인지'로 줄여서도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gas cooktop; it is often shortened to 레인지.

phrases.en: The new house has an electric stove.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불 없이 전기로 열을 내는 조리대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cooktop that heats with electricity instead of a flame.

phrases.en: Please heat the cold rice in the microwave for 2 minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 말에서 '레인지'는 보통 전자레인지를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In this phrase 레인지 usually means a microwave.

explain_en: 레인지 is a short form of both 가스레인지/전기레인지 (a cooktop) and 전자레인지 (a microwave), so '레인지에 돌리다' usually means heating food in the microwave. To refer to a cooktop without confusion, it is safer to add a word first, as in 가스레인지 or 전기레인지.

examples.ko: 잘 구운 햄버거에 달걀 반숙을 올려 아침으로 먹었어요.
examples.en: I put a soft-cooked egg on a well-grilled hamburger and had it for breakfast.
Do you like your eggs soft-cooked or hard-cooked?

examples.ko: 반숙 노른자가 밥에 흘러서 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: The runny yolk of a soft-cooked egg flows onto the rice and makes it tastier.
I only eat eggs cooked soft.
I put a soft-cooked egg in the ramen.

examples.ko: 반숙은 시간이 조금만 길어져도 완숙이 돼요.
examples.en: A soft-cooked egg becomes hard-cooked if the time runs just a little longer.

explain: 달걀을 노른자가 덜 익게 삶거나 부칠 때 써요. 반대말은 '완숙'이고, 식당에서는 '반숙 프라이'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I put a soft fried egg on my rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 집에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common at restaurants and at home.

phrases.en: I eat my eggs soft-cooked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달걀을 어떻게 익혀 먹는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says how you like your eggs cooked.

phrases.en: I like fully cooked better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반숙의 반대말이고, 노른자까지 다 익힌 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 반숙; the yolk is fully cooked.

explain_en: Used when an egg is boiled or fried so the yolk stays runny. The opposite is '완숙', and restaurants say things like '반숙 프라이'.

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 못 먹는 아이도 백김치랑 밥은 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Even a child who can't eat spicy food eats white kimchi with rice well.

examples.ko: 백김치는 고춧가루를 쓰지 않아서 맵지 않아요.
examples.en: White kimchi doesn't use chili powder, so it isn't spicy.
White kimchi goes well with these noodles.
Before the holiday, Mom made white kimchi.
The white kimchi broth is refreshing, so I keep drinking it.
Pear and chestnut go into white kimchi.

explain: 빨간 배추김치와 달리 고춧가루 없이 담근 하얀 김치예요. 맵지 않아서 아이나 매운 음식을 못 먹는 사람에게 권하기 좋아요. 보통 '백김치를 담그다·먹다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: My mother made white kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김치를 만드는 일은 '담그다'라고 하고, 백김치에도 똑같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Making kimchi is '담그다', and it is used the same way for white kimchi.

phrases.en: The white kimchi broth is refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 백김치는 맵지 않고 깔끔한 맛을 '시원하다'고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: White kimchi isn't spicy, and its clean, cool taste is described as '시원하다'.

phrases.en: I ate noodles together with white kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 음식과 곁들여 먹는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when eating it as a side with other food.

explain_en: Unlike red napa cabbage kimchi, this is white kimchi made without chili powder. It isn't spicy, so it is good to offer to children or people who can't eat spicy food. You say '백김치를 담그다' or '먹다'.

examples.en: My mother makes white porridge every morning.
I made porridge for my sick younger sibling.

examples.ko: 팥죽을 쑤는 날에는 온 가족이 모여요.
examples.en: On the day red bean porridge is made, the whole family gathers.

examples.ko: 쌀을 불린 다음에 죽을 쑤면 부드러워요.
examples.en: If you soak the rice before making porridge, it turns out soft.
Grandmother cooked paste and put up the wallpaper.

examples.ko: 죽을 쑤고 나서 소금으로 간을 해요.
examples.en: After making the porridge, I season it with salt.

explain: 쑤다는 죽·풀·묵처럼 곡식 알갱이나 가루를 물에 끓여 걸쭉하게 만들 때만 써요. 밥은 '짓다', 국은 '끓이다'라서 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: I completely botched this exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 시험을 망쳤을 때 비유로 써요. 죽처럼 형체 없이 흐트러졌다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a test or task goes badly, as if it turned to mush.
phrases.en_equiv: to make a mess of it

explain_en: 쑤다 is used only for boiling grain or flour in water into something thick, like porridge, paste, or jelly. Rice is '짓다' and soup is '끓이다', so the verb changes.

examples.en: Sprinkling sesame seeds on seasoned greens makes them nuttier.
They press sesame seeds for oil to make sesame oil.

examples.ko: 김밥 위에 참깨가 솔솔 뿌려져 있어요.
examples.en: Sesame seeds are lightly sprinkled over the gimbap.
I bought a bag of sesame seeds at the market.
The aroma of sesame gets stronger when it is toasted.
The salad with sesame dressing is delicious.

explain: '참깨'로 짠 기름이 '참기름'이고, 비슷하게 생긴 '들깨'에서는 '들기름'이 나와요. 요리할 때는 그냥 '깨'라고 줄여 말하는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: Roasting sesame seeds makes them smell better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 전에 깨를 볶는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for roasting sesame before cooking.

phrases.en: I sprinkled roasted sesame seeds on the bibimbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 볶아 놓은 깨를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to sesame that has already been roasted.

phrases.en: I sprinkle a little sesame on top of the food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참깨'를 줄여서 일상에서 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 참깨 used in everyday talk.

explain_en: Oil pressed from '참깨' is '참기름', while the similar-looking '들깨' gives '들기름'. When cooking, people often shorten it to just '깨'.

examples.en: In America, people eat turkey on Thanksgiving.
I saw a turkey up close for the first time on a farm.

examples.ko: 칠면조 구이는 크기가 너무 커서 혼자 못 먹어요.
examples.en: Roast turkey is too big to finish alone.
The turkey spread its tail wide.

examples.ko: 한국에서는 칠면조 고기를 파는 곳이 드물어요.
examples.en: In Korea, few places sell turkey meat.

examples.ko: 크리스마스 영화에는 칠면조 요리가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Turkey dishes often appear in Christmas movies.

explain: 미국의 추수감사절 음식으로 많이 알려져 있어요. 한국에서는 평소에 잘 먹지 않아서 영화나 뉴스에서 더 자주 들어요. '칠면조 고기', '칠면조 구이'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Turkey meat is a little tougher than chicken.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칠면조'만 말할 때는 새를 가리키고, '칠면조 고기'는 먹는 고기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '칠면조' alone can mean the bird; '칠면조 고기' means the meat you eat.

phrases.en: We ate roast turkey at the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오븐에 통째로 구운 요리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the dish of a whole turkey roasted in an oven.

phrases.en: Many people make turkey dishes at Christmas.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칠면조 구이'보다 넓게, 칠면조로 만든 음식 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than '칠면조 구이'; it covers any dish made with turkey.

explain_en: It is best known as the Thanksgiving dish in America. In Korea people rarely eat it day to day, so you hear it more in movies and news. You say 칠면조 고기 or 칠면조 구이.

en: to unfreeze; to defrost; to thaw

examples.en: I thawed the frozen meat last night.
I thawed the shrimp and put it in the fried rice.

examples.ko: 냉동 만두는 해동하지 말고 바로 쪄요.
examples.en: Don't thaw frozen dumplings; steam them right away.
I know how to defrost bread in the microwave.

examples.ko: 국물은 천천히 해동해야 맛이 덜 변해요.
examples.en: If you thaw broth slowly, the taste changes less.
I put the frozen rice on a plate to thaw it.

explain: '~을 해동하다'로 쓰고 대상은 보통 냉동식품이에요. '고기를 해동하다', '밥을 해동하다'처럼요. 구어체로는 '녹이다'도 써서 '냉동 만두를 녹여요'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I thawed the frozen dumplings and fried them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구어체로 쓰는 쉬운 말로, 얼린 음식을 풀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple colloquial word for thawing frozen food.

phrases.en: I thaw the rice in the microwave and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방법을 말할 때 '-(으)로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)로 when stating the method.

phrases.example: 저녁에 쓸 고기를 미리 해동해 놓았어요.
phrases.en: I thawed the meat in advance for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 쓰려고 먼저 해 두는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form meaning to do it ahead for later use.

explain_en: It takes an object, usually frozen food: '고기를 해동하다', '밥을 해동하다'. In casual speech '녹이다' also works, as in '냉동 만두를 녹여요'.

examples.en: My house is a short distance from school.
I walk for short-distance trips.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 근거리에 있는 가게를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This app shows stores that are nearby.
Short-distance buses have cheap fares.
The office is close, so I get there quickly.
I sent the photo through short-range communication.

explain: 반대말은 '원거리'예요. 가까운 곳에 갈 때는 '가까운 거리'라고 더 많이 말하고, '근거리'는 '근거리 통신', '근거리 이동'처럼 설명이나 안내문에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I send photos by short-range communication.
phrases.nuance_ko: 블루투스처럼 가까운 거리에서 쓰는 기술을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for technology like Bluetooth that works at close range.

phrases.en: For long-distance travel, I take the train.
phrases.nuance_ko: 근거리의 반대말로, 먼 거리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 근거리, meaning a long distance.

phrases.en: It looks clearer from up close.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 가까운 거리에서 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에서, it describes something done at a short distance.

explain_en: The opposite is 원거리 (long distance). In everyday speech people say 가까운 거리 more often; 근거리 shows up in fixed terms like 근거리 통신 (short-range communication) and in notices or explanations.
